scenes.heading: Reproductive strategies
scenes.sub: Copy yourself, or mix genes with a partner?
scenes.say: Every species must reproduce. Some simply copy themselves, while others combine genes from two parents. Which strategy is better? It depends on the environment.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: One set play vs a full playbook
scenes.science: Asexual: fast clones. Sexual: slower, but genetically diverse
scenes.breaks: A coach chooses the plays. Variation comes from meiosis, fertilisation and mutation, and natural selection acts on it.
scenes.say: A footy team with one set play does great, until the opposition works it out. Then it fails every time. That's asexual reproduction: fast and cheap, but every offspring is a clone. A full playbook takes more effort, like sexual reproduction. But when things change, some plays still work. That's genetic diversity.

scenes.heading: Asexual vs sexual
scenes.say: Asexual reproduction needs one parent. It's fast and cheap, but offspring are clones, so it suits stable environments. Sexual reproduction is slower and costs more energy, but crossing over, independent assortment and random fertilisation make every offspring unique.

scenes.heading: Types of asexual reproduction
points: Binary fission: bacteria split in two
scenes.say: There are five types of asexual reproduction. Bees Buzz From Violet Petunias. Binary fission, budding, fragmentation, vegetative propagation, like strawberry runners, and parthenogenesis, where an unfertilised egg develops.

scenes.heading: Binary fission
scenes.question: A bacterium divides every 20 minutes. Starting with one cell, how many cells are there after 3 hours?
scenes.say: A bacterium divides every twenty minutes. How many cells after three hours? That's one hundred and eighty minutes, so nine doublings. Two to the nine gives five hundred and twelve cells, all genetically identical.
scenes.caption: A bacterium divides every 20 minutes. How many cells after 3 hours? That's 180 minutes, so 9 doublings. 2⁹ gives 512 cells, all genetically identical.

scenes.heading: Cloning by SCNT
steps: Take a body cell from the donor
Remove the nucleus from an egg
Embryo grows; implant in a surrogate
scenes.say: Mammals can be cloned by somatic cell nuclear transfer. Take a body cell from the donor. Remove the nucleus from an egg. Put the donor nucleus in, and the embryo goes into a surrogate. The nucleus decides: the clone matches the nucleus donor. Dolly the sheep, born in nineteen ninety-six, was made this way.
scenes.caption: Mammals can be cloned by somatic cell nuclear transfer. Take a body cell from the donor. Remove the nucleus from an egg. Put the donor nucleus in, and the embryo goes into a surrogate. The nucleus decides: the clone matches the nucleus donor. Dolly the sheep, born in 1996, was made this way.

scenes.say: Quick recap. Asexual reproduction is fast and cheap, but makes clones. Sexual reproduction is slower but creates genetic diversity, which helps populations survive disease and change. And in SCNT, the nucleus decides. Now try the practice questions!
